note: Packs the media shows. 'printed' is what the pack says; verdicts come from the real /api/check at render time, never from this file.

packs.title: Artheget EZ, registered and consistent
packs.story: A registered antimalarial comes back green: no problems found, with the caveat.
packs.provenance: Product, strength, reg. no. and holder are NAFDAC Greenbook's real record (A4-6238). Batch and expiry are the team's demo values (shared/fixtures/demo-packs.json).

packs.title: Cloned registration number
packs.story: MedCheck catches a real NAFDAC number printed on a different product.
packs.provenance: Demo scenario from shared/fixtures/demo-packs.json: Artheget EZ's real number (A4-6238) on a pack named Malacure Forte. The pack is invented to show the attack; the registry record is real.

packs.title: Pack on NAFDAC Public Alert 042/2026
packs.story: MedCheck catches a batch NAFDAC seized in Kano and cites the alert.
packs.provenance: Every value is from NAFDAC Public Alert No. 042/2026 (19 Aug 2026).

packs.title: AquaMal QS, photographed
packs.story: A real AquaMal QS pack photographed in the app. MedCheck finds a product listing for B4-0910 but no current NAFDAC registration in its snapshot, so it says check with a pharmacist instead of overclaiming.

packs.provenance: Transcribed from the photo Eric supplied (front panel only: name, strength, ingredients, NAFDAC Reg. No. B4-0910). Manufacturer, batch and expiry are not visible on that side, so they are left empty.

packs.title: Natrilix SR, three photos
packs.story: Three photos of a real Natrilix SR pack. MedCheck flags it: the pack expired in Aug 2025, NAFDAC lists 04-8509 as Inactive, and the maker on the pack differs from the registered holder.

End flap (partly under a sticker): batch 32417, MFD 3/2023, EXP 8/2025; batch and expiry are a best reading, so the stand-in marks them below 0.8 and the user confirms them.
